questions.prompt: What does True or False give?
questions.explain: or needs only one side to be true.

questions.prompt: What is the value of bool(0)?
questions.explain: Zero is falsy. So are empty strings, empty lists and None.
Both sides must hold, so x lies between them. Python also lets you write this as 5 < x < 10.

questions.prompt: Why is `if x == True:` usually written `if x:`?
choices: x is already a boolean, so the comparison adds nothing
questions.explain: If x is already True or False, comparing it to True is a step that changes nothing.
